title: Shell completions for skillz CLI
description:
## Summary

Add shell completion support for the `skillz` CLI so users can tab-complete commands, subcommands, flags, and (where practical) dynamic values.

## Motivation

Discoverability and speed of use for a multi-subcommand CLI. Completions are a standard expectation for developer tools.

## Scope

- Generate and install/document completions for commonly supported shells, at least:
  - bash
  - zsh
  - fish (commonly supported alongside bash/zsh via clap_complete)
- Consider also: elvish, powershell if cheap via the same generator
- Likely approach: clap + `clap_complete` (workspace already uses clap 4 derive)
- Expose a stable UX, e.g. `skillz completions <shell>` (or equivalent) that prints the script to stdout for users to source/install
- Document how to enable completions for each supported shell

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] User can generate completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish
- [ ] Completions cover top-level commands and subcommands/flags
- [ ] README or man/help docs explain how to install/enable completions per shell
- [ ] Completions stay in sync with the clap command tree (generated, not hand-maintained)

## Notes

Keep this small: generation + docs first; dynamic value completion (skill names, library paths) can be a follow-up if not trivial.
close_reason: Met AC: skillz completions for bash/zsh/fish (+ elvish/powershell) via clap_complete; README install notes

title: library import --name to catalog under a different skill name
description:
## Goal
Allow `skillz library import` to record an Upstream Catalog Entry under a name different from the discovered skill directory name (e.g. keep existing `taste-skill` and import GitHub `…/skills/taste-skill` as `taste-skill-main`).

## Acceptance
- CLI: `skillz library import SOURCE --name NEWNAME`
- Only valid when exactly one skill is selected/discovered; otherwise clear error
- Source string still pins the GitHub path/rev; only the catalog `name` changes
- Collision/owned checks use the override name
- Regression test covers rename-past-collision
close_reason: Added library import --name and single-skill path discovery

title: Spec: Library setup, Local skills, and migrate recommender
description:
## Problem Statement

skillz's Library bootstrap and "bring existing skills under management" flows are hard to learn and unsafe in places: `library init`/`register` overlap oddly, `library list` doubles as catalog browse, `library import` soft-skips name conflicts, `--user` appears on commands where it does nothing useful, `project import` collides with `library import`, and unmanaged Installations are always Drift even when the user wants Project- or user-global-only skills that should never enter a Library. Users need a clear Library setup surface, an honest **Local** management state (especially authored membership without content Locks), and a top-level **migrate** recommender that uses Skillfile hints, bound Catalogs, and disk content to propose attach / overwrite / publish / keep-Local actions—with fail-closed defaults and a VCS cleanliness gate so migrate cannot overwrite dirty tracked skill files.

## Solution

Ship a coherent **Library admin + scope bootstrap + Local + migrate** slice (everyday verbs like `add`/`fetch`/`libcommit` rename deferred):

1. **Library commands:** tighten `init`/`register`, drop `library add` alias, reject `--user`, remove `name` from `library.toml`, add `version`, split `library list` (registry) vs `library catalog`, make `library import` fail-closed on conflicts with `--on-conflict fail|skip|prompt`, require `--move` to relocate root-level skills into `skills/`, improve help with commented examples.
2. **Bootstrap:** keep `project init` / `user init` as Binding twins (no adopt at init); reject nonsensical `--user`; keep Project-only `hooks`; rename the old Project Skillfile importer into top-level **`skillz migrate`**.
3. **Local skills:** first-class managed state that is not Drift and is not a Library Catalog Entry. Local authored = membership only (no content Lock). Local + `github:`/`cmd:` source = membership + real provenance/pin.
4. **`skillz migrate`:** plan/apply recommender over on-disk skills + optional Skillfile + bound Catalogs; prompt by default; `-i` TUI; `--no-prompt` only when determinate; `--dry-run`; VCS skills_dir cleanliness gate; partial apply OK.

## User Stories

1. As a skillz user, I want `library init` to create a new Library skeleton and register it, so that I can start a personal or team catalog quickly.
2. As a skillz user, I want `library init` on a directory that already has skills under `skills/`, so that I can turn an existing layout into a Library without inventing files by hand.
3. As a skillz user, I want `library init --move` when skill dirs sit at the Library root, so that skillz relocates them under `skills/` only when I explicitly allow moves.
4. As a skillz user, I want `library init` without `--move` to error if root-level skills need relocating, so that I am not surprised by filesystem moves.
5. As a skillz user, I want `library init` to refuse a path that already has `library.toml` and tell me to `register`, so that init vs register stay distinct.
6. As a skillz user, I want `library register` to require an existing Library (`library.toml` present) and only update my machine registry, so that cloning a Library checkout is a pure register step.
7. As a skillz user, I want `library register --read-only`, so that I can bind a company Library without write expectations.
8. As a skillz user, I want no `library add` alias, so that "add" is not confused with installing Catalog Entries into a Project.
9. As a skillz user, I want `skillz library … --user` to error, so that I do not think Library admin is scoped to user-global Installations.
10. As a skillz user, I want `library.toml` without a `name` field, so that the shared Binding/registry name is authoritative and register never fails on name mismatch.
11. As a skillz user, I want `library.toml` to carry a `version` property, so that skillz can migrate schema safely later.
12. As a skillz user, I want legacy `library.toml` files with `name` and/or missing `version` to load via migration, so that existing Libraries keep working.
13. As a skillz user, I want `library list` to show only the machine registry, so that I can see name, path, rw/ro, and VCS at a glance.
14. As a skillz user, I want `library catalog [-l NAME] [-t tag]`, so that I can browse Catalog Entries without a Managed Project.
15. As a skillz user, I want `library catalog` to default to the registered Library covering cwd when `-l` is omitted, so that working inside a Library checkout is convenient.
16. As a skillz user, I want `library import` to bulk-add Upstream Catalog Entries from GitHub without installing into any Project, so that my Catalog can grow independently of Installations.
17. As a skillz user, I want `library import` to abort the entire import by default when any name conflicts (Owned, different Upstream identity, or duplicate discovery names), so that I never get a partial silent Catalog.
18. As a skillz user, I want `--on-conflict skip` on `library import`, so that I can import the non-conflicting subset deliberately.
19. As a skillz user, I want `--on-conflict prompt` to ask about each conflict in turn (stable order), so that I can skip or rename per conflict before an atomic apply.
20. As a skillz user, I want same-identity Upstream refresh and identical skips to succeed under fail-closed import, so that re-running import to update pins remains safe.
21. As a skillz user, I want `-l` as a short alias for `--library` on Library catalog/import (and migrate where applicable), so that common flags are ergonomic.
22. As a skillz user, I want richer `--help` with contrasted, commented examples on Library commands, so that I can learn init vs register vs import vs catalog without reading the README.
23. As a developer, I want `project init --binding` (and `--bind`) with optional `--skills-dir`, so that a repo becomes a Managed Project with ordered Library Bindings.
24. As a developer, I want `project init` not to adopt or rewrite existing skills, so that leftovers stay unmanaged until migrate.
25. As a user, I want `user init --binding`, so that `~/.agents/skills` uses the same Binding/Lock model without a Project.
26. As a user, I want `skillz project … --user` and `skillz hooks … --user` to error, so that I cannot mis-scope Project-only or hooks operations.
27. As a developer, I want `hooks show` / `hooks install` on Managed Projects only, so that Drift gates attach to repo VCS (git XOR jj).
28. As a developer, I want `skillz status` / `status --user` after init, so that I can verify Bindings and skills_dir.
29. As a developer, I want top-level `skillz migrate` (and `migrate --user`), so that unmanaged → managed uses one command for both scopes.
30. As a developer, I want migrate to auto-detect Skillfile unless `--ignore-skillfile`, so that origins inform recommendations without a separate importer command.
31. As a developer, I want Skillfile rows with no on-disk Installation skipped with a warning, so that migrate never fetches materializations I did not already place.
32. As a developer, I want `migrate --dry-run` to print the full plan (signals + recommended action) without writes, so that I can review safely.
33. As a developer, I want migrate to refuse to start if tracked files under `skills_dir` are dirty in git/jj, so that skillz cannot overwrite uncommitted skill edits.
34. As a developer, I want other dirty paths (e.g. new `.skillz/` after init) to be allowed during that gate, so that bootstrap + migrate can happen in one working session.
35. As a developer, I want untracked skills under `skills_dir` allowed by the gate, so that brand-new unmanaged trees can be migrated.
36. As a jj user, I want migrate to run `jj status` before planning so the working copy is snapshotted, so that reads/writes see a consistent tree.
37. As a developer, I want migrate to compare each on-disk skill to bound Catalog names and Skillfile origins and recommend attach / use-Library-files / publish-to-Library / Local authored / Local+source / no-op, so that I am not inventing the workflow.
38. As a developer, I want prompt mode by default for ambiguous skills, so that unclear cases do not silently guess.
39. As a developer, I want each prompt to allow answering for this skill or for all remaining skills in the same situation class, so that large trees are not tedious.
40. As a developer, I want `migrate -i` to review the same plan in a TUI, so that I can batch-confirm actions.
41. As a developer, I want `migrate --no-prompt` to apply only when every skill is determinate from flags + safe auto-rules, otherwise abort with no writes, so that scripts stay fail-closed.
42. As a developer, I want `--authored` to default “no Catalog match, no source” outcomes to Local authored, so that Project-only skills are easy to claim.
43. As a developer, I want partial apply if I cancel mid-prompt/`-i`, so that already-confirmed skills remain managed.
44. As a developer, I want Local authored skills recorded as membership only (no content hash Lock), so that Project VCS owns file history and skillz only stops Unlocked Drift.
45. As a developer, I want Local + real `github:`/`cmd:` source tracked for provenance/refresh without a Library Catalog Entry, so that scope-only Upstream-like skills are honest.
46. As a developer, I want `migrate NAME --source …` to set Local+source for unmanaged or Local authored (and update Local+source), so that I can attach provenance one skill at a time.
47. As a developer, I want `migrate NAME --source` to refuse unsafe conversions from Library-backed Locks without an explicit detach path, so that I do not accidentally drop Library linkage.
48. As a developer, I want migrate recommendations when a Catalog Entry already exists under the same name—even if Skillfile also provides a source—so that attach vs content mismatch vs source-identity mismatch are all handled.
49. As a developer, I want migrate to abort or prompt when Skillfile/source identity disagrees with an existing Upstream Catalog identity for the same name, so that conflicting origins are never papered over.
50. As a developer, I want later movement from Local to Library to distinguish **attach** (Lock to existing Catalog Entry) vs **publish** (push Installation content into Library), so that “Library already has this skill” is first-class (full everyday rename of publish/attach may land later; migrate must already expose both outcomes).
51. As an agent authoring docs, I want commented help examples for migrate and Library bootstrap, so that humans and agents share one teaching sequence.
52. As a skillz maintainer, I want this slice to leave everyday verb renames (`libcommit`→publish/push, absorb `fetch`, etc.) out of scope, so that the change set stays shippable.

## Implementation Decisions

### Scope boundary

- In scope: Library admin CLI/behavior, `library.toml` schema (`version`, drop `name`), Local membership model, `project init` / `user init` / hooks `--user` rejection, replace `project import` with top-level `skillz migrate` (+ `--user`), help/examples for these commands.
- Out of scope: renaming `libcommit`/`fetch`/`add` everyday verbs; binding edit after init; `library unregister`; content-hash Drift for Local skills; fetching Skillfile-only missing skills.

### Domain: Local

- **Local** = managed in the current scope (Managed Project or user-global) without a Library Catalog Entry.
- **Local authored:** record membership only (name ∈ local set). No content hash Lock. Not Drift.
- **Local + source:** membership + real `github:…` or `cmd:…` (with pin/tool version as for Upstream). No Library Entry. Default: no content-hash Drift for Local (authored or sourced).
- Moving Local → Library later: **attach** to existing Catalog Entry vs **publish** content into Library; version mismatch choices: refresh from Library, publish local as newer, or abort. Migrate must recommend these; dedicated everyday command names can follow in a later spec.

### `library.toml`

- Fields: `version` (integer; current = 1), `upstream` entries as today; **no `name`**.
- Load path: missing `version` ⇒ treat as legacy (0); accept and ignore legacy `name` on read; writes emit `version = 1` without `name`.
- Refuse unsupported future `version` with a clear error.

### Library init / register

- **`init`:** create-or-adopt Library at path + register `--name` into registry.
  - Missing/empty → skeleton (`library.toml` + `skills/`) + register.
  - Existing `library.toml` → error; suggest `register`.
  - Skills already under `skills/*/SKILL.md` only → ensure meta + register (no `--move`).
  - Root-level `*/SKILL.md` present → error unless `--move`, which relocates those dirs into `skills/` then registers.
  - Ambiguous junk → error.
- **`register`:** path must exist and already be a Library (`library.toml` required). Do **not** invent meta. Optional `--read-only`. Registry `--name` is authoritative (no name compare to file).
- Remove visible `add` alias for `register`.
- Reject `--user` with an error on all `library` subcommands.

### Library list / catalog / import

- **`library list`:** registry only.
- **`library catalog`:** Catalog Entries; `-l`/`--library`; `-t` tags; cwd Library default when `-l` omitted.
- **`library import`:** GitHub → Upstream Catalog only; no Project Installation; document that clearly.
- Conflicts (Owned name, different Upstream identity, duplicate names in one discovery): default **fail entire import** (classify all first; write nothing; print all conflicts).
- `--on-conflict fail|skip|prompt` (default fail). Prompt = sequential per conflict; skip or type new catalog name; apply atomically after all resolutions (or abort).
- Non-conflicts: Add, Update same identity, SkipIdentical.
- Reject `--user` on import/list/catalog.

### Bootstrap

- `project init` / `user init` unchanged in spirit; reject `--user` on `project` and `hooks`.
- No adopt at init.
- No binding-edit commands in this slice.
- Remove or deprecate `project import` in favor of `skillz migrate` (compat alias optional briefly).

### Migrate: inputs and gates

- Command: `skillz migrate` [options] [NAME] [--source SOURCE]; scope via absence/`--user`.
- Before plan (when git or jj detected at scope root):
  - **jj:** run `jj status` to snapshot.
  - Fail if any **tracked** path under `skills_dir` is modified/deleted vs HEAD/`@-`.
  - Allow dirty paths outside `skills_dir`; allow **untracked** under `skills_dir`.
  - No VCS → skip gate (optional warn).
- Skillfile: auto-detect unless `--ignore-skillfile`. Rows with no on-disk `SKILL.md` Installation → skip with warning (do not fetch).
- Inspect on-disk skills in `skills_dir` only for actionable rows.
- Signals per skill: management state; Skillfile source (if any); Catalog matches across Bindings (none / single / ambiguous); for Owned Catalog trees content identical|differs; for Upstream Catalog entries source identity match|mismatch vs Skillfile or Local source when present; uncompared when no Owned tree and no source to compare.

### Migrate: recommendation matrix

Only skills **on disk** are actionable. “Catalog match” means same skill name in a bound Library Catalog. “Skillfile source” means a Skillfile row for that name (and not `--ignore-skillfile`).

#### A. Unmanaged + on disk

| # | Skillfile source | Catalog match | Content / identity | Recommended action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | none | none | n/a | **Local authored** (default under `--authored` or “authored for this class”) |
| A2 | present | none | n/a | Prompt/flags: **Local + source** (use Skillfile source) **or** **publish Upstream** into writable Binding |
| A3 | none | single, Owned | identical | **Attach** (Library Lock; keep files) |
| A4 | none | single, Owned | differs | Prompt: **use Library files** (overwrite local) **or** **publish local → Library** **or** **keep Local authored** |
| A5 | none | single, Upstream | uncompared (no Owned tree) | Prompt: **Attach** Upstream Lock (optionally refresh Installation from source) **or** **keep Local authored** |
| A6 | present | single, Owned | identical | **Attach** (Skillfile origin is advisory; content already matches Library) |
| A7 | present | single, Owned | differs | Prompt: **use Library files** **or** **publish local → Library** **or** **Local + Skillfile source** (keep local content, record provenance, do not attach) — do not silently discard Skillfile origin |
| A8 | present | single, Upstream | Skillfile identity **matches** Catalog Upstream identity | **Attach** Upstream (refresh optional); Skillfile confirms origin |
| A9 | present | single, Upstream | Skillfile identity **mismatches** Catalog Upstream identity | **Conflict** — prompt: keep Local+Skillfile source **or** attach Catalog Upstream (overwrite/reinstall from Catalog source) **or** abort skill; never merge identities silently |
| A10 | any | ambiguous (multiple Bindings / differing entries) | any | **Conflict** — prompt to pick Library Binding/entry or abort; `--no-prompt` → abort run |

Notes:
- A6–A9 explicitly cover **unmanaged + Catalog match + Skillfile source** (omitted from the earlier short matrix).
- If Skillfile source present and user chooses Library attach while content differs (A7), prefer explicit overwrite-from-Library or publish-to-Library over attach-keeping-divergent-files without a Lock hash story.

#### B. Already managed + on disk

| # | State | Signals | Recommended action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Library-locked, clean vs Lock | any Skillfile/Catalog | **No-op** (report on dry-run) |
| B2 | Library-locked, Drift (hash mismatch) | Catalog exists | Out of primary migrate auto-fix in this slice — report “already managed; use drift workflow”; do not invent repair unless easily identical to A4 choices under explicit prompt |
| B3 | Local authored | Catalog match identical | Suggest **attach** (optional upgrade from Local → Library Lock) |
| B4 | Local authored | Catalog match differs | Same choices as A4 (use Library / publish / stay Local) |
| B5 | Local authored | Skillfile or user `--source` | Eligible for **Local + source** conversion via `migrate NAME --source` or prompt |
| B6 | Local + source | Catalog Upstream identity match | Suggest **attach** |
| B7 | Local + source | Catalog identity mismatch / Owned differs | Same conflict/prompt patterns as A7/A9 |
| B8 | Local + source | no Catalog | **No-op** unless `--source` updates pin |

#### C. `migrate NAME --source`

| # | Current state | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Unmanaged | → Local + source |
| C2 | Local authored | → Local + source |
| C3 | Local + source | Update source/pin |
| C4 | Library-backed | **Refuse** unless explicit detach flag (detach not required in this slice — refuse with message) |
| C5 | NAME omitted / multiple names | Error — exactly one NAME |
| C6 | Catalog has same name with **different** Upstream identity | Prompt or fail — do not silent overwrite Catalog; Local+source without attach is allowed if user confirms |

#### D. Non-actionable

| # | Case | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Skillfile-only, no files | Skip + warning |
| D2 | Empty skills_dir, no Skillfile | Dry-run says nothing to do; apply no-op success |

### Migrate: interaction modes

- Default: **prompt** (CLI Q&A) for non-determinate skills; safe auto-apply for determinate no-brainers (e.g. A3/A6 identical attach, B1 no-op) may apply without asking unless `--dry-run`.
- `-i` / `--interactive`: TUI over the same plan.
- `--no-prompt`: only flags + safe auto-rules; any unclear skill → abort entire run, no writes (stricter than partial prompt cancel).
- `--dry-run`: plan only.
- `--authored`: default class for A1-like rows → Local authored.
- `--ignore-skillfile`: drop Skillfile signals (A2/A6–A9 degrade to A1/A3–A5).
- Partial apply: OK when user cancels mid-prompt/`-i` after some confirms.
- “This skill” vs “all remaining in this situation class” on prompts; flags may pre-seed those class answers.

### CLI help

- Every command in this slice gets improved about text + `after_help` examples with comments contrasting sibling commands.
- Reject nonsensical `--user` with an explicit error message naming the correct invocation (`user init`, or omit the flag).

### Modules / interfaces (no file paths)

- Extend Library meta load/save for `version` and nameless schema; migrate legacy.
- Adjust init skeleton + `--move` adoption; tighten register.
- Add catalog subcommand wiring; narrow list.
- Import conflict policy API (`fail`/`skip`/`prompt`) with atomic apply.
- Persist Local membership (+ optional source) in scope config or lockfile structure without requiring content hash for authored Local.
- New migrate planner producing structured per-skill signals + recommended action + alternatives; applier executing attach / overwrite-from-library / publish-to-library / set-local / set-local-source.
- Reuse existing Catalog listing, content hash, github source identity, Skillfile parse, and libcommit/attach primitives where they already exist; prefer extending `App` over new subsystems.
- CLI: clap definitions, help, `--user` rejection helpers, Ratatui prompt/`-i` for migrate and import conflicts.

### Architectural notes

- Attach vs publish remain distinct outcomes inside migrate even if everyday command renames land later.
- Do not reintroduce fake `github:local/import/…` sources.
- ADR 0002 still applies: Local is honest scope ownership, not dishonest Library Drift.
- ADR 0005: Tool-Provided stays `cmd:…` Upstream-shaped source strings; Local+`cmd:` does not create a third Library EntryKind.

## Testing Decisions

- Test **external behavior** through `App` (and CLI help/rejection where cheap): registry files, `library.toml`, skills tree layout, lock/membership records, migrate plan structs, and apply side effects—not clap private fields or TUI rendering details.
- **Primary seam:** `App` Library APIs, init/register/move, import with conflict policies, Local membership, migrate plan + apply, `project_init`/`user_init`, hooks/`--user` rejection at CLI or App boundary as appropriate.
- Prefer one seam (`App`); avoid new test-only facades.
- Prior art: existing `skillz-core` fixture tests for `library_init`/`library_register`/`library_import`, `project_init`, `user_init`, Skillfile import, drift unlocked reasons—extend those patterns for Local (unlocked → not drift when membership set), init `--move`, import fail-closed, and migrate matrix cases (at least one test per matrix row A1–A10, plus C1–C4 and VCS gate behavior with temp git/jj fixtures where feasible).
- Golden/help tests optional for critical `--help` examples; not required for every string.

## Out of Scope

- Everyday verb redesign (`libcommit`→publish/push, absorb `fetch` into `add --source`, `promote` auto re-Lock, top-level `remove`, `skillz skill`→`self`).
- Editing Bindings after init; removing Libraries from registry; deleting Catalog Entries.
- Auto-fetching Skillfile skills not on disk.
- Content-hash Drift enforcement for Local skills.
- Full everyday `attach`/`publish` command naming polish beyond migrate outcomes (may be stubbed as App methods).
- Changing Binding URL identity model or multi-machine registry sync beyond existing behavior.
- Implementing the older `docs/cli-simplification-proposals.md` items outside this slice.

## Further Notes

### Test seam (confirmed for implementers)

Implement and test via **`skillz_core::App`** as the single primary seam; CLI remains a thin adapter. Interactive Ratatui flows can wrap the same plan/apply APIs.

### Teaching sequence (help/README later)

```bash
skillz library init ~/code/personal-skills --name personal
skillz library register ~/code/acme-skills --name company --read-only
skillz library list
skillz library catalog -l personal
skillz library import github:owner/skills -l personal --dry-run

cd ~/code/my-app
skillz project init --binding company:ro --binding personal
skillz hooks install
skillz migrate --dry-run
skillz migrate -i

skillz user init --binding personal
skillz migrate --user --authored
```

### Matrix coverage checklist for implementers

Ensure planner fixtures cover A1–A10 (including Skillfile+Catalog combinations A6–A9), B1–B8 as applicable, C1–C6, D1–D2, skills_dir dirty tracked failure, jj snapshot preamble, and `--ignore-skillfile` degrading A2/A6–A9.

### Related doc

Informational prior art: `docs/cli-simplification-proposals.md` (broader CLI review). This spec is the authority for the Library + bootstrap + Local + migrate slice.

## Parent

z-3fe — Spec: Library setup, Local skills, and migrate recommender

## What to build

Users can create or adopt a Library with a clear init vs register split: `library.toml` carries `version` (no `name`); `init` scaffolds or adopts (with `--move` when root-level skills must relocate into `skills/`); `register` only wires an existing Library into the machine registry; the `library add` alias is gone; nonsensical `--user` on these commands errors; help shows commented examples contrasting init vs register.

- [ ] `library.toml` writes `version = 1` and omits `name`; legacy files with `name` and/or missing `version` still load
- [ ] Unsupported future `version` fails with a clear error
- [ ] `library init` creates skeleton + registers; refuses path that already has `library.toml` (suggest register)
- [ ] `library init` adopts existing `skills/*/SKILL.md` layout without `--move`
- [ ] Root-level `*/SKILL.md` requires `--move` to relocate into `skills/`; without `--move`, errors
- [ ] `library register` requires existing `library.toml`; does not invent meta; supports `--read-only`
- [ ] No visible `library add` alias for register
- [ ] `library init|register … --user` errors with a clear message
- [ ] Help includes contrasted commented examples; App-level tests cover the behaviors above

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

title: library import fail-closed + --on-conflict
description:
## Parent

z-3fe — Spec: Library setup, Local skills, and migrate recommender

## What to build

`library import` bulk-adds GitHub Upstream Catalog Entries with fail-closed conflict handling: default abort entire import on name conflicts; `--on-conflict fail|skip|prompt` (prompt walks conflicts one-by-one, then applies atomically). title: Spec: Everyday verbs (add/publish/update/remove)
description:
## Problem Statement

Day-to-day skillz commands are hard to learn: overlapping materialize verbs (`add` / `fetch` / `new`), an opaque `libcommit` that both first-catalogs and Branch-Locks, a `promote` + `lock --main` dance that fights real review workflows, and no clear split between “send Project → Library,” “link an on-disk skill to a Catalog Entry,” and “refresh Project from Library.” Everyday commands must also respect **Local** management and Library **`contribution = direct | review`** without requiring `--as` / `--source` on publish when the Project already records how a skill is managed.

## Solution

Redesign the everyday CLI (no command aliases / back-compat shims; lockfiles stay compatible or migrate):

1. **Materialize / link from Catalog via `add`:** plain `add NAME` installs from Catalog when missing; **`add --attach`** links an existing on-disk skill to a Catalog Entry; **`--from-library`** takes Catalog files when linking (or when replacing). Also `add --source` (stage; optional `--local`) and `new` (scaffold; optional `--local`). Drop `fetch` and drop a separate **`attach`** command.
2. **Project → Library:** single verb **`publish`** (multi-name = one review branch unit). Default **auto** create-vs-update per name; **`-u/--update`** = all must already exist; **`--create-only`** = all must be new. Infer Owned vs Upstream (and Upstream source) from **existing Project management state** — no `--as` / `--source` on publish. Refuse unmanaged skills. Notify about sibling dependencies not in the batch. On **`contribution = review`**, push the branch to the Library remote by default and **open a PR/MR by default** (best-effort via host CLI); print clear copy-pasteable next steps. Escapes: `--no-push`, `--no-pr`.
3. **Library → Project refresh:** **`update`** refreshes Installation + Lock from Library main tip (fetch/remote-aware). Not overloaded onto `add --attach`.
4. **Drop `promote`.** `contribution` on `library.toml` drives direct-to-main vs review Branch Lock; pending review is **visible** but does not fail hooks; review Libraries require merge-commit-only history policy.
5. **Hygiene:** top-level `remove`; keep **`skillz skill`** (do not rename); improve `status` / `list` / `tag` / `drift` help; Drift `-i` vocabulary matches new verbs.
6. **Agent usability:** rewrite the embedded skillz skill as the non-interactive playbook; add `--json` on inspect/plan/publish-result commands; non-TTY defaults that never block on prompts; stable exit codes; structured pending vs Drift; copy-paste remediation in errors.

Companion epic **z-3fe** owns Library admin, Local persistence, and migrate.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want `skillz add NAME` to install from a bound Catalog with a Lock when the skill is not on disk, so that collaborators get an honest Installation.
2. As a developer, I want plain `add NAME` to error if the skill directory already exists, with a hint to `--attach` or `--from-library`, so that I do not silently overwrite or mis-link.
3. As a developer, I want `skillz add NAME --attach -l L` to Lock an existing on-disk skill to a Catalog Entry without publishing Project content into the Library, so that linking and installing share one verb.
4. As a developer, I want `skillz add NAME --attach --from-library` when trees differ, so that I can take Library files at link time.
5. As a developer, I want `skillz add --source …` to stage Upstream files into `skills_dir`, so that I do not need a separate `fetch` command.
6. As a developer, I want `skillz new NAME` to scaffold Authored skills, so that creation stays distinct from acquisition.
7. As a developer, I want `--local` on `new` / `add --source` to mark Local authored or Local+source immediately, so that scope-only skills are not Unlocked Drift.
8. As a developer, I want unmanaged `new` / `add --source` (without `--local`) to remain Unlocked until migrate/Local/`add --attach`/`publish` prerequisites are met, so that try-then-manage still works.
9. As a developer, I want `publish` to refuse skills that are not already managed in the Project, so that Catalog kind/source always comes from Project state.
10. As a developer, I want `publish` to infer Owned vs Upstream (and Upstream source / cmd pin) from Local membership or existing Library Lock, so that I do not pass `--as` or `--source`.
11. As a developer, I want default `publish A B C -l L` to create Entries for new names and update existing ones in one branch unit, so that dependent skills can ship together.
12. As a developer, I want `publish -u A B C` to fail if any name is missing from the Catalog, so that update-only batches are safe.
13. As a developer, I want `publish --create-only A B` to fail if any name already exists in the Catalog, so that create-only batches are safe.
14. As a developer, I want `publish` to detect sibling dependencies of the named skills and notify me (prompt/suggest including them), so that units stay coherent.
15. As a developer, I want `publish` on a `contribution = direct` Library to write Library main and Lock to that tip, so that personal Libraries need no review ceremony.
16. As a developer, I want `publish` on a `contribution = review` Library to use one Branch Lock branch for the batch and record pending review until the locked rev is an ancestor of main, so that merge-commit review works.
17. As a developer, I want `publish` on a review Library to **push the branch** to the Library remote by default, so that Branch Lock SHAs are reachable for collaborators and pending checks.
18. As a developer, I want `publish` on a review Library to **open a PR/MR by default** when a host CLI is available (`gh` / `glab` / equivalent), so that review starts without a separate forge step.
19. As a developer, I want `--no-push` and `--no-pr` to opt out of push or PR/MR creation, so that offline or custom forge workflows still work (with warnings when Lock won’t be useful remotely).
20. As a developer, I want `publish` output to list clear next steps with **copy-pasteable commands** (view PR, merge guidance, `skillz update` after merge, fetch/status), so that I know what to do without reading docs.
21. As a developer, I want pending Branch Locks to show clearly in `status` / drift reporting without failing `drift --check`, so that Projects can ship temporary Branch Locks to collaborators.
22. As a developer, I want review Libraries documented/enforced as merge-commit-only (detect squash fallout when Lock rev never becomes an ancestor of main), so that Branch Lock SHAs remain meaningful.
23. As a developer, I want skillz to fetch Library `origin` (or configured remote) or otherwise consult the remote before branch bases and pending/merged checks, so that stale local checkouts do not lie.
24. As a developer, I want `update NAME…` to refresh Installation + Lock from Library main tip, so that “get latest from Library” stays distinct from first-time `add` / `add --attach`.
25. As a developer, I want no `promote` command, so that review finish is pending-clear via merge ancestry plus optional `update` to main tip.
26. As a developer, I want `remove NAME` to drop Installation, Lock, and Local membership while leaving Catalog Entries, so that cleanup is discoverable.
27. As a developer, I want `skillz skill show|install` kept under that name, so that Tool-Provided templates stay stable.
28. As a developer, I want Drift `-i` actions named with `publish` / `add --attach` / `update` / `remove`, so that interactive Drift matches the CLI.
29. As a developer, I want commented help contrasting `add` vs `add --attach` vs `publish` vs `update`, so that direction of data flow is obvious.
30. As a skillz maintainer, I want no CLI aliases for removed commands (`fetch`, `libcommit`, `promote`, `attach`, `lock --main`), so that users learn one surface; lockfiles remain loadable (migrate if needed).
31. As an agent, I want the embedded `skillz` skill docs to match the z-g97 command surface (no `libcommit`/`promote`/`fetch`), so that I follow the correct workflows.
32. As an agent, I want a short decision-tree playbook in that skill (edit → Local vs Library-backed → `publish` / `add --attach` / `update`; prefer `new --local` for Project-only), so that I do not create Unlocked Drift by default.
33. As an agent, I want `--json` on `status`, `drift`, `list` / `list --catalog`, `migrate --dry-run`, and `publish` results (including branch, PR URL, `next_steps`), so that I can parse outcomes without scraping tables.
34. As an agent, I want non-TTY (or explicit `--no-prompt`) runs to never open Ratatui or block on “this skill / all remaining” prompts, so that unattended runs finish.
35. As an agent, I want dependency and conflict notifications to print remediation and exit or require `--with-deps` / `--no-deps` rather than waiting on stdin, so that CI/agent sessions do not hang.
36. As an agent, I want stable exit codes distinguishing usage errors, hard Drift (`drift --check`), and success (pending review must not fail hooks), so that I can branch on status.
37. As an agent, I want `status --json` (and drift JSON) to expose `pending_review` separately from hard Drift, so that I can report Branch Lock state without treating it as a gate failure.
38. As an agent, I want errors to include the exact next command to run (`publish -u`, `add --attach`, `new --local`, …), so that retries are idempotent and obvious.
39. As an agent, I want `publish --dry-run` to show the planned branch/push/PR actions without network side effects, so that I can confirm before mutating remotes.
40. As an agent, I want publish to skip PR creation cleanly when forge auth is missing (still push by default) and print copy-paste `gh`/`glab` next steps, so that lack of `gh` auth is not a hard failure.
41. As an agent, I want the skill to list which paths to commit (Installation tree + `.skillz/skillz.lock` / user lock), so that I do not leave Lock and files out of sync in VCS.

## Implementation Decisions

### Compatibility

- **CLI:** no backward-compatible command aliases. Remove or hard-error old verbs with a short “use X” message only if the binary still hits a deleted name during transition builds; prefer clean cut in the shipped surface described here.
- **Lockfiles / Local membership / `library.toml`:** remain readable across versions; add `contribution` with default **`direct`** when missing; migrate lockfile schema only if required.

### Library `contribution`

In `library.toml`:

```toml
version = 1
contribution = "direct" # or "review"
```

- **`direct`:** `publish` writes Library **main** and Locks the Project to that tip. No pending review state.
- **`review`:** `publish` writes a **single branch** for the invocation’s skill set, Branch-Locks each skill to the unit tip rev, marks **pending** until (after remote fetch) that rev is an **ancestor of main**. Policy: **merge commits only** (no squash/rebase-and-merge). If a “merged” PR leaves Lock rev ∉ main ancestry, surface a clear error/recovery (`update` or re-`publish`).
- Store policy on the **Library**, not the Binding.

### `publish` on `review` Libraries: push, PR/MR, next steps

After committing the unit on the Library branch:

1. **Push** the branch to the Library remote (`origin` or configured) **by default**, so Lock SHAs exist centrally.
2. **Open a PR/MR by default** (best-effort): prefer host CLIs such as `gh pr create` / `glab mr create` when available and authenticated; if unavailable or it fails, **publish still succeeds** after push and the output explains how to open the PR manually.
3. Escapes: **`--no-push`** (local branch only; warn that collaborators cannot resolve the Lock until pushed); **`--no-pr`** (push but skip forge PR/MR).
4. **`direct` Libraries:** no branch push/PR path (write main + Lock tip only).

**Output (required):** end with a short “Next steps” section that includes copy-pasteable commands tailored to what happened, for example:

- Link or command to view/open the PR/MR when created
- If PR was not created: exact `gh` / `glab` / compare-URL instructions for this branch
- Reminder to use **merge commit** (not squash/rebase-and-merge) on `review` Libraries
- After merge: e.g. `skillz update NAME…` if they want Project Lock/files at main tip; `skillz status` / drift to see pending clear after fetch
- If `--no-push`: exact `git push -u origin BRANCH` (or jj equivalent) from the Library checkout path

### `add` (install, stage, and link)

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `add NAME` [`-l`…] | Catalog → Installation + Library-backed Lock when skill **not** on disk; **error if** skill dir already exists (hint `--attach` / `--from-library`) |
| `add NAME --attach` [`-l`…] | Require on-disk skill + Catalog Entry; set Library-backed Lock; clear Local membership; do **not** publish Project tree into Library |
| `add NAME --attach --from-library` | As `--attach`, and overwrite Installation from Catalog when content differs (or always take Catalog files) |
| `add --source SOURCE` [NAME] [`--local`] | Stage github/path/cmd materialization; `--local` ⇒ Local+source |
| `new NAME` [`--local`] | Scaffold; `--local` ⇒ Local authored membership |
| `fetch` / standalone `attach` | Removed (`add --source` / `add --attach`) |

`--attach` and plain install are mutually exclusive modes of `add`. `--from-library` is only valid with `--attach` (or a documented replace path); not a substitute for day-to-day **`update`**.

### Managed prerequisite for `publish`

`publish` accepts only skills **managed** in the current scope:

- Local authored, or
- Local + source (`github:` / `cmd:`), or
- Already Library-backed (Lock present)

**Refuse Unlocked / unmanaged** with guidance to `--local`, `migrate`, or `add --attach` first.

**Infer Catalog action from management state:**

| Project state | Create (new Catalog name) | Update (name exists) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local authored | Owned Entry from Installation files | If Catalog name already exists → **error** (suggest `add --attach` or resolve naming); do not silently overwrite Library content from Local-only |
| Local + source | Upstream Entry using recorded source + pin | Same: name exists → error suggest `add --attach` |
| Library-backed Owned | — | Write Installation content to Library (main or review branch) + refresh Lock |
| Library-backed Upstream | — | Edited Installation ⇒ Overlay Fork / Owned path on writable Library (Upstream Catalog stays reference unless Forked) |

**Auto summary:** create when Local_* and Catalog miss; update when Library-backed and Catalog hit; Local_* + Catalog hit ⇒ error toward `add --attach`.

### `publish` flags

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| (default) | Per name: create or update per rules above; mixed allowed when creates are Local-new and updates are Library-backed |
| `-u` / `--update` | Every name must already be an updatable Library-backed (or Catalog-existing update) case; fail if any would create |
| `--create-only` | Every name must create; fail if any Catalog name exists |
| `-l` / `--library` | Target writable Binding |
| `-m` / `--message` | Commit/branch message |
| `--no-push` | Review only: do not push branch (warn) |
| `--no-pr` | Review only: push (unless `--no-push`) but do not open PR/MR |

No `--as`. No `--source`.

Default for review: **push on**, **PR/MR on** (best-effort).

Multi-name ⇒ **one branch** (review) or one main commit unit (direct) for all skills in the invocation. Dependency check: notify/suggest adding detected sibling deps not in the name list (prompt in interactive; print warnings otherwise; optional `--with-deps` later).

### `update` / remove

- **`update NAME…`**: Fetch/consult Library remote; set Installation + Lock to **main tip** for that Entry (Library → Project). Distinct from `publish -u` and from `add --attach`.
- **No `promote`.** No standalone **`attach`.**
- **`remove NAME`**: Installation + Lock + Local membership; Catalog unchanged; soft-warn dependents.

### Remote freshness

Before branch creation, pending/merged ancestry checks, and `update`:

- Fetch Library remote (`origin` or configured) into the registered checkout, **or** otherwise read remote refs/objects so decisions use current central state.
- If Lock SHA missing locally → fetch until present or error clearly.

### Pending visibility

| State | Hooks `drift --check` | UX |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unlocked / hash mismatch | Fail | Drift |
| Review Branch Lock, rev not ancestor of main | **Pass** | **Pending review** (visible) |
| Rev ancestor of main | Pass | Pending cleared; may still offer `update` if behind tip |

### Dropped / kept commands

- Drop: `fetch`, `libcommit`, `promote`, standalone `attach`, ceremonial `lock --main` (prefer **only `update`** for advancing to main tip).
- Keep: `skillz skill`, `status`, `list`, `tag`, `drift`, `hooks`, Library/project/user admin per z-3fe.

### Help / agent skill

- Comment examples for `add` / `add --attach` / `publish` / `update` directions; Drift `-i` labels aligned.
- **Rewrite embedded skill** (`skillz skill show` / install payload) as the authoritative agent playbook for this surface (see Agent usability).

### Agent usability

Assume many edits are performed by coding agents that have the skillz skill installed. Requirements:

#### Embedded skill playbook (required)

- Replace all obsolete verbs (`fetch`, `libcommit`, `promote`, `lock --main`, standalone `attach`).
- Include a short decision tree and non-interactive recipes only.
- Prefer documenting **`new --local`** / **`add --source … --local`** for agent-authored scope-only skills.
- Document commit set: skill files under `skills_dir` + Project/user lockfile.
- Document pending review vs hard Drift and that hooks fail only on hard Drift.
- Document `publish` push/PR defaults and `--no-pr` / `--no-push` for agent environments.

#### `--json` (required on inspect / plan / publish result)

Human text remains default. Support `--json` for at least:

- `status`
- `drift` (and `drift --check` machine summary)
- `list` / `list --catalog`
- `migrate --dry-run`
- `publish` (result: skills, library, contribution mode, branch, remote, pr_url if any, `next_steps[]`)

JSON must expose **`pending_review`** separately from hard Drift items.

#### Non-interactive behavior (required)

- When stdin is not a TTY, or `--no-prompt` is set: never enter Ratatui / blocking multi-choice prompts.
- Dep / conflict notices: print guidance; use `--with-deps` / `--no-deps` (or equivalent) rather than y/N waits.
- `publish` PR default remains on, but missing forge auth ⇒ skip PR, succeed after push, print copy-paste open-PR commands (same spirit as human next-steps output).
- Optional later: `SKILLZ_AGENT=1` bundles non-interactive preferences; not required if non-TTY detection is solid.

#### Exit codes (required)

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Success |
| 1 | Usage / hard operational error |
| 2 | Hard Drift when using `drift --check` (hooks) |

Pending review alone must **not** use code 2. Optional distinct code for pending-only checks may wait; prefer JSON fields.

#### Errors and dry-run

- Failures name the exact remediation command(s).
- Support `publish --dry-run` (and keep migrate `--dry-run`) for plan-without-side-effects.

#### Out of scope for agent ergonomics

- A second parallel “agent CLI”
- Renaming `skillz skill`
- Requiring forge auth for successful `publish`

### Modules

- Extend `App` only (one seam). Wire clap. Reuse Local membership, Catalog, VCS helpers; add contribution policy + pending detection + publish batching + update-from-main; implement link path as `add` flags rather than a separate command.

## Testing Decisions

- Test via **`skillz_core::App`**: `add` install vs exists-error vs `--attach` / `--from-library`; publish auto/`-u`/`--create-only`; refuse unmanaged; infer kind from Local/Lock; multi-skill one branch; dep notification; direct vs review; review publish schedules push + PR attempts (testable via seams/fakes); `--no-push`/`--no-pr`; next-step message content; pending ancestry after fetch; `update` refresh; `remove`; no promote / no standalone attach API in the happy path.
- Agent ergonomics: `--json` shapes for status/drift/list/migrate dry-run/publish result; non-TTY / `--no-prompt` does not block; `drift --check` exit code 2 only for hard Drift; embedded skill text contains current verbs (smoke/string asserts OK); `publish --dry-run` performs no push/PR.
- Prior art: libcommit/promote/fetch tests rewritten to publish/update/`add --attach` semantics.
- Fixture Libraries with `contribution = review` and merge-commit history; assert squash fallout detection message when ancestry fails.

## Out of Scope

- Re-specifying migrate / library init (z-3fe).
- Enforcing GitHub/GitLab branch-protection APIs for merge-commit-only (document + detect fallout).
- Supporting every forge beyond best-effort `gh` / `glab` (manual next-step commands cover the rest).
- Per-name different Upstream sources in one `publish` invocation (split invocations; same-branch continue may be a follow-up flag).
- CLI back-compat aliases.
- Renaming `skillz skill`.

## Further Notes

### Seam

`skillz_core::App` + thin CLI.

### Teaching examples

```bash
skillz add ecto-thinking
skillz new my-hack --local
skillz publish my-hack -l personal --create-only
skillz publish grilling domain-modeling -l company -u -m "unit"
# review Library: pushes branch, opens PR/MR when gh/glab available, prints next steps
skillz publish grilling -l company -u -m "unit" --no-pr   # push only
skillz add other -l personal --attach --from-library
skillz update ecto-thinking
skillz remove old-skill
skillz skill show
skillz status --json
skillz drift --json
skillz publish grilling -l company -u -m "unit" --dry-run
```

### Agent playbook (also in embedded skill)

```text
Library-backed edit → publish NAME -l LIB -u -m "…"
  (review: push+PR; after merge, pending clears; optional update NAME)
New Project-only skill → new NAME --local → edit → publish … --create-only when sharing to Library
Link existing on-disk skill to Catalog → add NAME --attach [-l LIB] [--from-library]
Refresh from Library main → update NAME
Never use libcommit/fetch/promote (removed)
```

### Related

- z-3fe (Library, Local, migrate) — blocker/companion
- `docs/cli-simplification-proposals.md` — historical notes only; this bead + amendments are authoritative for everyday verbs

title: Spec: skillz — skills manager CLI/TUI
description:
## Problem Statement

I work across many projects, each with its own set of agent skills. Some skills are Upstream (from other people's GitHub repos), some are Authored by me, some are Forked (started Upstream or Tool-Provided, then tweaked), and some arrive as Tool-Provided globals from tools I install. When I start a new project I often copy skills by hand. That is messy: I forget where a skill lived, copies diverge across Managed Projects, and if I keep skills only as laptop globals, collaborators on a Project never get them. I want a single tool — **skillz** — that keeps Libraries as the union catalog of skills I (or my team/company) use, lets Managed Projects select and Lock Installations from those Libraries, and makes discovery, updates, Drift, and Promote straightforward — including a workplace flow where Library review can lag Project shipping.

## Solution

**skillz** is a CLI (with a future TUI) that replaces Skillfile in my workflow. It manages one or more Libraries (Personal, team, or company), registers Managed Projects (and a user-global `~/.agents/skills` scope) with ordered Library Bindings, and uses Locks so lasting Installations track Catalog Entries. Day-to-day editing and new-skill tryout happen **in the Project (or user) skills directory**; **`libcommit`** formalizes tested Installations into the Library workflow (new Catalog Entry, Library Branch Lock, or Overlay Fork). Discovery includes `skillz list --tag TAG`. git pre-commit and `jj push-with-checks` gate publishing Drift unless explicitly allowed. External Projects are observe/import only. Install scope is intentionally narrow — not Skillfile parity.

Agreed command-level usage is in `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md` and summarized under **Usage Flows** below.

## User Stories

1. As a solo developer, I want a Personal Library that is the union of skills I keep via libcommit from Managed use, so I always know what I standardize on.
2. As a solo developer, I want to record Authored Skills as Owned Entries, so my custom skills have a source of truth outside any one Project.
3. As a solo developer, I want Upstream Skills as Catalog Entries (source + Lock) without owning their content, so the Library stays a complete union without vendoring the internet.
4. As a solo developer, I want to Fork an Upstream or Tool-Provided skill into an Owned Entry when I edit it for keeps, so my tweaks are first-class Library content.
5. As a solo developer, I want Tool-Provided skills left out of the Library until I libcommit/promote them, so globals do not silently pollute the catalog.
6. As a library owner, I want to assign Tags to Catalog Entries, so I can discover skills by topic or toolchain.
7. As a library owner, I want `skillz list` (with filters such as `--tag TAG`), so I can find skills without remembering which Project last used them.
8. As a library owner, I want to search/list across bound Libraries for a Managed Project, so selection respects binding order and availability.
9. As a developer, I want to register a Project as Managed with an ordered list of Library Bindings, so skillz knows where Catalog Entries may come from.
10. As a developer, I want Library Bindings to be read-only or writable, so I can install from a company Library without being able to mutate it.
11. As a developer, I want to try a newly authored or fetched skill in my Project first, then `libcommit` it into a Library, so I test before the union catalog changes.
12. As a developer, I want skillz to materialize an Installation and record a Lock after add/libcommit, so the Project has pinned, reproducible skill content.
13. As a developer, I want Installations committed in the Project repo, so collaborators receive skills on clone without needing my Libraries.
14. As a collaborator, I want to clone a Managed Project and have skill files present, so agents work without running skillz first.
15. As a developer, I want to bump a Lock and reinstall when a Library entry advances, so Projects stay intentionally current.
16. As a developer, I want a Drift Report across Managed Projects, so I can see Installations that disagree with their Locks or with Library main line.
17. As a developer, I want Drift gates and reports to offer libcommit / Branch Lock / Overlay Fork / Promote as explicit next actions, so nothing silently merges into a Library.
18. As a developer, I want to Promote a skill change into a writable Library main line, so lasting shared edits land in the right source of truth.
19. As a developer in a workplace, I want `libcommit` to create a Library Branch Lock from my tested Installation, so I can ship the Project before main-line approval with an honest Lock.
20. As a developer in a workplace, I want a report of Managed Projects whose Locks are not on Library main line, so pre-merge usage is visible.
21. As a developer with a fully read-only Library, I want Overlay Fork into a writable bound Library via libcommit, so I can still ship Project-local skill changes honestly.
22. As a developer, I want External Projects (other people's clones) to be observable without forced Library membership, so skillz does not rewrite foreign repos.
23. As a developer, I want to explicitly import a skill from an External Project into a Library, so useful finds can join the union on purpose.
24. As a team lead, I want a shared team or company Library using the same skillz model, so the workplace uses one tool shape.
25. As a team member, I want my Managed Project to bind company → team → personal with precedence, so name conflicts resolve predictably.
26. As a Library maintainer, I want Promote / libcommit into a company Library to require an explicit writable target, so personal drift never silently writes company content.
27. As a developer starting a new Managed Project, I want to select skills already in Libraries via skillz list/add, so I stop hand-copying from old Projects.
28. As a developer, I want the Project skills directory to default to `.agents/skills` but be overridable (e.g. `.claude/skills`), so skillz fits my agent layout.
29. As a developer, I want to manage `~/.agents/skills` with the same skillz model (`skillz user …`), so user-global skills are not a separate ad-hoc mess.
30. As a developer migrating from Skillfile, I want import (including `-i` TUI adopt) into Catalog Entries + Locks, so I can leave Skillfile behind.
31. As a developer, I want a CLI named `skillz` as the primary interface, so I learn one tool.
32. As a developer, I want a future TUI over the same command API, so discovery, import adopt, and Drift review are pleasant.
33. As a developer, I want `skillz status` for a Managed Project or `--user`, so I can see Bindings, Installations, Locks, and Drift at a glance.
34. As a developer, I want `skillz list --tag` to accept repeated flags and comma-separated lists, so filtering matches how I think about Tags.
35. As a developer, I want list to show all Binding matches in precedence order by default, with optional `--dedupe`, so I can see overlays.
36. As a developer, I want list/add to show Availability across Project, user-global, and other agent skill roots (e.g. `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`), so I know what the agent can already load.
37. As a developer, I want `add` to no-op/refresh when already in the Project and to warn when a skill exists only in user/other roots, so I do not assume collaborators see it.
38. As a developer, I want `skillz add --tag …` and `-i` multi-select, so I can pull many Library skills at once.
39. As a developer, I want `skillz fetch github:owner/repo SKILLNAME` to find nested skills, so Pocock-style layouts work.
40. As a developer, I want warnings (and `--with-deps`) when a skill references sibling skills (e.g. grill-with-docs → grilling, domain-modeling), so dependency graphs are less surprising.
41. As a developer, I want git pre-commit to block committing drifting skill files unless I allow Drift, so testing locally does not accidentally publish dishonest Locks.
42. As a developer on jj, I want `jj push-with-checks` (not `skillz push`) to drift-check before `jj git push`, so ordinary pushes stay normal and skill gates sit at the share boundary.
43. As a developer, I want `libcommit` as the verb that turns a tested Installation into Library + Lock state, so edit/add/new share one formalization step.
44. As an agent implementing skillz, I want one application command API as the test seam, so CLI and TUI share behavior.
45. As a Library owner, I want Libraries themselves to be ordinary versioned repos, so review/branch/PR workflows reuse existing source control.
46. As a developer, I want skillz to refuse to treat a Project as Managed until Bindings are configured, so External vs Managed stays explicit.
47. As a developer, I want to remove a skill from a Managed Project (Installation + Lock) without deleting it from the Library, so Projects can drop skills while the union catalog remains.
48. As a developer, I want to see which Managed Projects use a given Catalog Entry, so impact of a Library change is visible before I bump Locks.
49. As a developer, I want failed installs/libcommits to leave Project state consistent, so recovery is clear.
50. As a workplace admin, I want read-only Bindings to still allow install and list, so consumers are not blocked from discovery.

## Usage Flows

Canonical transcripts: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.

### A — Library bootstrap
`library init` / `library add` / `library list`. Registry is **user-global** name → local path. Committed Project Bindings use shared **name + remote URL**. VCS inferred (`.jj/` → jj, else git).

### B — New Managed Project
`project init --bind …` writes Bindings + empty Locks; default `--skills-dir .agents/skills` (overridable). No skills installed yet. Hooks installed.

### B2 — User-global scope
`user init --bind …` manages `~/.agents/skills` with the same model; config/Locks in user skillz state.

### C — Convert existing Project
`project import --dry-run` / `--from skillfile` / `--adopt-local` / `-i` TUI per-skill upstream|authored|skip. Keep matching files; leftovers are Drift candidates. `user import` for home skills.

### D — Discovery
`list` with `--library` / `--user` / `--tag` (repeated and/or comma-separated, AND). Default: show all Binding hits in precedence order; `--dedupe` optional. Show **Availability**: Project `skills_dir`, user-global `~/.agents/skills`, and other known agent skill roots (e.g. `.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`) even when they are not the install target.

### E — Add
- **E1** already in Library: `add` / `add --tag` / `-i` / `--with-deps`. Respect Availability: already in Project → no-op/refresh; only in user/other roots → warn that collaborators need a Project install.
- **E2/E3** new Upstream or Authored: **Project-first** via `fetch` / `new` into skills dir → test → **`libcommit --as upstream|authored`** into a writable Library (creates Catalog Entry + Lock). Until libcommit = Drift.

### F — Edit / libcommit / Promote
Edit Installation in place; `libcommit` → Branch Lock or Overlay Fork + update Lock; `promote` → Library main; `lock --main` after merge. git pre-commit blocks Drift; jj uses **`jj push-with-checks`**. Escape: `--allow-drift` / `SKILLZ_ALLOW_DRIFT=1`. No `skillz push` as jj entrypoint.

## Implementation Decisions

### Product name and interfaces
- Tool name: **skillz**. v1 CLI; TUI later on the same application command API.
- Replace Skillfile (ADR 0001); narrow install scope; no Skillfile parity.

### Domain rules
- Library = union catalog (Owned + Upstream references) for skills you libcommit/keep.
- Managed Project Bindings: ordered name+url+writability; local registry resolves path.
- Installations committed in Project skills dir (default `.agents/skills`).
- User-global scope: `~/.agents/skills`.
- Edit/new tryout in Installation; **libcommit** formalizes; **Promote** = main-line.
- Branch Lock primary; Overlay Fork fallback (ADR 0002).
- Drift never silent-synced.

### Discovery and deps
- Tags; list filters; no default dedupe.
- **Availability** column/flags on `list` / `add`: Project `skills_dir`, `~/.agents/skills`, plus known agent roots (`.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.claude/skills`, …). Single install target remains `skills_dir`.
- Dep heuristics including Pocock `grill-with-docs` pattern; `--with-deps`.

### Metadata (ADR 0003)
- Project: `PROJECT/.skillz/skillz.toml` + `skillz.lock`; Installations in `skills_dir` (default `.agents/skills`).
- User registry: `~/.config/skillz/registry.toml` (Library name→path; Managed Project paths for Drift).
- User scope: `~/.config/skillz/user.toml` + `user.lock`; Installations in `~/.agents/skills`.
- Library repo: `library.toml` + Owned trees under e.g. `skills/`.
- Upstream `source`: `github:owner/repo[/path][@rev]` string in CLI and TOML (not structured fields).

### Architecture / test seam / stack (ADR 0004)
- Rust binary + `skillz-core` lib (application command API = test seam) with temp filesystem fixtures.
- `clap`; TOML via `toml`/`toml_edit`; shell out to `git`/`jj`.
- TUI later: `ratatui` + `crossterm`; not FrankenTUI for v1; thin UI boundary for a possible later swap.
- Libraries as normal git/jj repos; skillz lock format (not Skillfile.lock).

### Hooks
- git pre-commit on skill paths.
- jj: repo-local alias `jj push-with-checks` only (not `skillz push`).

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior of the application command API with fixture Libraries + Managed Projects (+ user-scope temp home).
- Cover: init/bind; import/-i; list tags & dedupe off/on; add from Library; fetch/new → libcommit; edit → libcommit Branch Lock; Overlay Fork; drift gates allow/deny; --with-deps warning path for grill-with-docs-like bodies; read-only library rejects libcommit target.
- CLI argv thin; TUI later. No prior art in-repo (greenfield).

## Out of Scope

- Skillfile coexistence layer; Skillfile-style long-lived patch pins as happy path.
- Silent cron sync into Libraries.
- Auto-Managing every clone under ~/code.
- Auto-import all Tool-Provided globals.
- Full multi-platform install matrix.
- Marketplace product; company auth beyond git hosting.
- TUI in the first vertical slice (API must allow it); FrankenTUI as v1 TUI backend.
- `skillz push` as the jj push command.
- Perfect dependency graphs from prose.

## Further Notes

- Glossary: `CONTEXT.md`.
- ADRs: `0001-replace-skillfile`, `0002-branch-lock-over-patches`, `0003-metadata-layout-and-source-strings`, `0004-rust-stack-ratatui-not-frankentui`.
- Usage/tech annex: `.scratch/skillz/usage-flows.md`.
- This repo uses jj + Beads (`br`, prefix `z`).
- Open polish: whether `libcommit` auto-chooses Overlay Fork vs requiring a flag; GitHub auth/`gh` vs raw git for private Upstream.

title: library import: bulk Upstream from GitHub repo
description:
## What to build

`skillz library import <source> --library <name>` discovers every skill (`**/SKILL.md`) in a GitHub repo (or nested path) and upserts **Upstream Catalog Entries** into that Library only. No Project or `--user` Installations/Locks.

### CLI

```bash
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal
skillz library import https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --library personal --dry-run
skillz library import github:mattpocock/skills --library personal --path skills/engineering
```

### Behavior

- Accept `github:owner/repo[/path][@rev]` **and** `https://github.com/owner/repo…` URLs; normalize to canonical `github:…@rev` in the catalog (ADR 0003).
- Clone/cache the repo (reuse existing fetch cache), walk for `SKILL.md`, skill name = containing directory name.
- Optional `--path <prefix>` limits discovery to that subtree (after optional source path).
- `--dry-run` lists what would be added/updated/skipped; writes nothing.
- Apply: upsert Upstream entries; identical source+name → no-op/skip; name collision with different source → report and skip (or error clearly — prefer skip+warn for bulk).
- Does **not** materialize into any Managed Project or user-global skills dir.
- Works against a registered Library by name (writable); does not require cwd to be a Managed Project.

### Acceptance

- [ ] `library import --help` documents source forms, `--library`, `--dry-run`, `--path`
- [ ] HTTPS and `github:` sources both work; catalog stores `github:…@rev` with per-skill path
- [ ] Importing `mattpocock/skills` (or a fixture tree) creates Upstream entries for each discovered skill
- [ ] `--dry-run` prints the plan and leaves `library.toml` unchanged
- [ ] `--path skills/engineering` imports only under that prefix
- [ ] No files appear under a Project/`--user` skills dir as a side effect
- [ ] Tests cover discovery, URL normalize, dry-run, path filter, collision skip
close_reason: Met AC: library import discovers github/https sources, dry-run/path/collision, catalog-only upsert + tests

title: Agent skill for managing skills with skillz (+ tool-provided install provenance)
description:
## Summary

Ship a skillz-authored skill that teaches agents how to use the `skillz` CLI to manage Libraries, Catalog Entries, Installations, Locks, Drift, and related workflows — and implement Tool-Provided cataloging per ADR 0005 so skillz can re-install from the providing tool instead of a Library mirror.

## Design

Resolved in grill (see Design field + ADR 0005 + CONTEXT.md). Tool-Provided → explicit libcommit → Upstream `cmd:` template reference; eager validate install + version probe at catalog time; Locks pin observational tool version; Project add always runs the template.

## Deliverables

1. `cmd:` / `|version:` Upstream source support + validation + materialize (ADR 0005)
2. Agent-facing skill documenting skillz workflows (including Tool-Provided cataloging once available)
design:
## Resolved (grill 2026-11-10)

Tool-Provided enters Library only on explicit libcommit as an Upstream reference (not Owned), unless later Forked.
No third EntryKind: extend Upstream source strings (ADR 0005).
Catalog source = command template, e.g. `cmd:rexpad skill install --dir {dir}`; skillz substitutes `{dir}` (never host paths in the string).
Optional `|version:…` override; default version probe is `{argv0} --version`.
`@rev` optional in catalog; required on Locks as observational tool version (ordering/newer), not content hash.
Eager validation at Library add/libcommit: confirm install template + version probe succeed (parallel to checking github when cataloging). Do not defer syntax/tool failures to Project add.
Project materialize/refresh always invokes the template; no Library mirror fallback; missing tool → clear error. Collaborators still use committed Project Installations.

See ADR 0005 and CONTEXT.md (Tool-Provided Skill, Upstream Skill).
acceptance_criteria:
Upstream cmd: source grammar with {dir} (and documented placeholders) plus optional |version:…
libcommit/catalog of Tool-Provided validates install + version probe before recording the Catalog Entry
Locks store observational tool version (@rev); catalogs may omit it
Project/user add from such an entry runs the template; missing tool fails clearly; no Library file mirror
CONTEXT.md + ADR 0005 remain accurate
Agent-facing skill documents how to manage skills with skillz (including Tool-Provided / cmd: cataloging when implemented)
notes: Design question resolved via grill-with-docs. Implementation should follow ADR 0005. Remaining work: cmd:/version grammar + validation + materialize path; plus the agent-facing skillz-management skill (may split).
close_reason: Met AC: cmd: Upstream sources + eager validation/materialize (ADR 0005); skillz agent skill authored
